privacy.title: Global Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Rumuze is not just a service provider; we are the architects of your digital existence. Specializing in bespoke software engineering, corporate identity formulation, and data-driven digital marketing, we handle your data with the same precision we apply to our code.

sections.title: 1. Introduction
sections.content: Welcome to Rumuze. We define the digital frontier. As a premier agency, we are committed to protecting the integrity of your personal information, proprietary software assets, and strategic brand data.

sections.title: 2. Information We Collect
sections.content:
To engineer your success, we collect specific data points:

• **Client Identity:** Name, corporate email, and business registration details required for contract initiation.
• **Brand Assets:** Logos, brand guidelines, and visual assets uploaded for design projects.
• **Marketing Data:** Access credentials for ad platforms (Meta, Google Ads) and analytics data needed for campaign optimization.
• **Technical Telemetry:** Usage logs, API calls, and error reports from software we develop or manage.

sections.title: 3. How We Use Your Data
sections.content:
Data is the fuel for your digital engine. We utilize it for:

• **Software Lifecycle Management:** Developing, testing, and deploying robust applications.
• **Campaign Optimization:** Analyzing market trends and user behavior to refine ad targeting and ROI.
• **Brand Strategy:** Crafting visual identities that resonate with your specific audience demographics.
• **Operational Security:** Protecting your intellectual property and our infrastructure.

sections.title: 4. Data Sharing & Disclosure
sections.content:
Your data stays within our ecosystem, except when:

• **Strategic Partners:** We collaborate with cloud providers (AWS, Vercel) and media platforms (Meta, Google) to execute your projects.
• **Legal Mandates:** We comply with strict legal requirements to protect our agency and clients.

sections.title: 5. International Data Transfers
sections.content: As a global entity, Rumuze may process your data in multiple jurisdictions. We rely on Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) and adequacy decisions to ensure your data remains protected regardless of borders, in full compliance with GDPR and CCPA frameworks.

sections.title: 6. Data Retention
sections.content:
We retain client data only as long as necessary to fulfill contractual obligations or legal requirements. 

• **Active Projects:** Retained for the duration of the service agreement + 1 year.
• **Financial Records:** Retained for 7 years for tax and audit compliance.
• **Marketing Data:** Anonymized or deleted upon contract termination.

sections.title: 7. Data Security
sections.content: We employ military-grade encryption for all client assets. Source code is stored in secure, private repositories. Marketing data is handled with strict role-based access controls (RBAC) to ensure confidentiality.

sections.title: 8. Your Privacy Rights
sections.content:
You retain full ownership of your intellectual property. You have the right to:

• **Access:** Review the data we hold on your projects.
• **Portability:** Request a transfer of your brand assets and code repositories.
• **Deletion:** Request removal of sensitive data upon contract termination, subject to retention laws.

sections.title: 9. Contact Us
sections.content:
For privacy concerns regarding your software or brand assets, contact our Legal Team:

**Email:** legal@rumuze.com
**Address:** Rumuze HQ, Global Tech Park.

terms.title: Master Services Agreement
terms.intro: These Terms constitute a binding Master Services Agreement (MSA) between Rumuze ('The Agency') and you ('The Client'). By engaging our services, you agree to these terms governing intellectual property, liability, and performance standards.

sections.title: 1. Scope of Engagement
sections.content: Rumuze agrees to provide software development, design, and marketing services as detailed in specific Statements of Work (SOW). This MSA governs all such SOWs and prevails over any conflicting terms in purchase orders.

sections.title: 2. Intellectual Property Rights
sections.content:
To ensure mutual protection of assets:

• **Client Ownership:** Upon full payment, the Client owns all 'Deliverables' created specifically for them (e.g., custom code, logos, campaign strategies).
• **Agency Background IP:** Rumuze retains all rights to its pre-existing code libraries, tools, frameworks, and methodologies used to create the Deliverables. The Client is granted a perpetual, non-exclusive license to use this Background IP within the scope of the project.

sections.title: 3. Confidentiality
sections.content: Both parties agree to hold all 'Confidential Information' (trade secrets, strategy documents, code repositories) in strict confidence. This obligation survives the termination of this Agreement for a period of five (5) years.

sections.title: 4. Payment & Commercial Terms
sections.content:
• **Invoicing:** Services are billed according to the SOW schedule. Invoices are due Net-30 from receipt.
• **Late Fees:** Overdue payments shall accrue interest at the lesser of 1.5% per month or the maximum rate permitted by law.
• **Suspension:** Rumuze reserves the right to suspend services for accounts more than 15 days overdue.

sections.title: 5. Warranties & Disclaimers
sections.content: Rumuze warrants that services will be performed in a professional manner in accordance with industry standards. EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED, ALL DELIVERABLES ARE PROVIDED 'AS IS'. WE DISCLAIM ALL IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY AND FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.

sections.title: 6. Limitation of Liability
sections.content: IN NO EVENT SHALL RUMUZE BE LIABLE FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES. OUR TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE TOTAL FEES PAID BY THE CLIENT IN THE SIX (6) MONTHS PRECEDING THE CLAIM.

sections.title: 7. Termination
sections.content:
• **For Convenience:** Either party may terminate an SOW with 30 days written notice, subject to payment for work completed.
• **For Cause:** Immediate termination permitted for material breach uncured after 10 days notice.

sections.title: 8. Governing Law
sections.content: This Agreement shall be governed by international commercial standards and the laws of the jurisdiction where Rumuze's invoicing entity is registered. Disputes shall be resolved through binding arbitration.

saudiPage.h1: Software Engineering & Performance Marketing for Saudi Enterprises
saudiPage.intro: Rumuze executes structured software engineering and performance marketing for enterprises operating in Saudi Arabia. We work with decision-makers who require defined governance, clear accountability, and outcomes tied to measurable performance criteria.
saudiPage.authorityStatement: Rumuze is a remote-first project execution partner for Saudi enterprises. Every engagement is governed by a documented statement of work, structured reporting cadence, and defined deliverable acceptance criteria.

execution.title: Digital Project Execution for Saudi Businesses
execution.body: Saudi enterprises require digital partners who operate with documented clarity. We begin every engagement with a structured discovery session that produces a written scope document — not a proposal deck. That document defines what will be built, what constitutes acceptance, what the timeline is, and what happens if scope changes. Project status is reported weekly in a written format appropriate for internal distribution to leadership. No milestone progresses without client sign-off. This is not a communication preference — it is a structural requirement of how we operate.
points: Written scope document produced before any development begins
Defined deliverables with documented acceptance criteria
Weekly written status reports structured for leadership distribution
Milestone sign-off required before phase progression

softwareDelivery.title: Structured Software Delivery Model
softwareDelivery.body: We engineer custom software systems — web platforms, enterprise applications, ERP integrations, and operational automation. Development is structured in two-week sprints, each beginning with a defined scope and ending with a client review session. Every sprint produces a written summary delivered within 24 hours of the review. Systems are architected to production standards from the first sprint: separate environments, version-controlled codebase, peer-reviewed code, and no production deployment without documented testing evidence. Maintainability is a contractual requirement, not an optional quality consideration.
points: Two-week sprint cycles with written scope per sprint
Sprint review with client and written summary within 24 hours
Separate development, staging, and production environments
No production deployment without documented testing evidence

marketing.title: Performance Marketing Measured Against Defined Acquisition Metrics
marketing.body: We execute performance marketing programs against predefined acquisition criteria. Every campaign is structured before launch around specific, agreed KPIs: cost per qualified lead, conversion rate by channel, customer acquisition cost, and revenue attribution by source. We do not manage campaigns on an open retainer. Campaigns run under a defined budget with weekly performance reports covering actual versus target metrics. If a channel is not performing against its defined benchmark by the agreed review date, we adjust or stop it. Marketing spend without attribution accountability is not something we accept on behalf of clients.
points: Campaign KPIs defined and agreed before any spend begins
Weekly performance reports: actual vs. target by channel
Budget-defined engagements — no open retainer without benchmarks
Underperforming channels adjusted or paused at agreed review intervals

governance.title: Governance, Reporting & Accountability
governance.body: We operate under a clear accountability structure. Project status is reported weekly. All deliverables are documented. Milestones require sign-off before progression. We provide a single point of contact for all projects, ensuring your team is never chasing updates or managing ambiguity. Contracts define scope, timelines, and success metrics before work begins.
points: Weekly project status reports delivered to stakeholders
Single point of contact for all project communications
Milestone sign-off process before phase progression
Defined contracts with scope, timelines, and KPIs

whyStructured.title: Why Saudi Companies Prefer Structured Execution Partners
whyStructured.body: Enterprise decision-makers in Saudi Arabia have encountered poorly governed digital projects: missed timelines, unclear deliverables, and no accountability when outcomes are not met. A structured execution partner operates differently. Scope is defined. Deliverables are documented. Reporting is consistent. Performance is measured against agreed benchmarks, not subjective assessment.
points: Defined scope eliminates scope creep and budget overruns
Documented deliverables create clear acceptance criteria
Consistent reporting reduces management overhead
Measurable performance creates accountable partnerships

enterpriseFramework.intro: Rumuze operates under a defined project governance and delivery model. This framework applies to all software engineering and performance marketing engagements regardless of project size.
enterpriseFramework.authorityStatement: The Rumuze Enterprise Delivery Framework defines governance, sprint cadence, reporting structure, SLA commitments, and technology standards for all client engagements.

governance.title: Governance & Architecture Model
governance.body: Every project is governed by a defined structure: a Project Owner on the Rumuze side, a client-designated point of contact, and a documented escalation path. Before any development begins, we establish a Statement of Work (SOW) that defines scope boundaries, deliverable acceptance criteria, and change request protocols. Architecture decisions are documented and require client review before implementation.
points: Defined project ownership and escalation path
Statement of Work established before development begins
Architecture decisions documented and reviewed
Change request protocol for scope modifications

lifecycle.title: Project Lifecycle Framework
lifecycle.body: Our project lifecycle consists of five phases: Discovery, Architecture, Development, Validation, and Deployment. Each phase has defined entry and exit criteria. No phase begins until the prior phase is formally closed. This prevents scope drift, reduces rework, and ensures client alignment at every stage.

phases.name: Discovery
phases.desc: Requirements gathering, scope definition, and feasibility assessment

phases.name: Architecture
phases.desc: System design, technology selection, and security planning

phases.name: Development
phases.desc: Sprint-based implementation with weekly deliverable reviews

phases.name: Validation
phases.desc: QA, performance testing, and client acceptance testing

phases.name: Deployment
phases.desc: Staged release, monitoring setup, and handover documentation

sprintCadence.title: Sprint & Delivery Cadence
sprintCadence.body: Development is structured in two-week sprints. Each sprint begins with a planning session defining the sprint scope and ends with a review session presenting completed work. Clients receive a written sprint summary after each review. Unfinished sprint items are re-evaluated before inclusion in the next sprint — no work is silently carried over without acknowledgment.
points: Two-week sprint cycles with defined scope per sprint
Sprint planning session at the start of each cycle
Sprint review with client at the end of each cycle
Written sprint summary delivered within 24 hours of review

accountability.title: Accountability & Reporting Structure
accountability.body: We maintain a consistent reporting cadence for all active engagements. Weekly status reports cover completed work, upcoming milestones, blockers, and budget consumption. Monthly executive reports summarize progress against the project plan and KPIs. All reports are delivered in a format appropriate for internal distribution to stakeholders and leadership.

reportTypes.covers: Sprint progress, blockers, next week's objectives, hours consumed
Project health, milestone status, KPI performance, risk register
Full delivery summary, performance benchmarks, handover documentation

riskSLA.title: Risk Mitigation & SLA Philosophy
riskSLA.body: All engagements include a risk register maintained throughout the project lifecycle. Risks are classified by probability and impact and reviewed weekly. Our service level commitments define response times, resolution targets, and escalation procedures. We do not offer SLA guarantees without documented scope — every commitment is tied to a defined deliverable and measured objectively.
slas: Critical issue response within 4 business hours
Standard support request resolution within 2 business days
Weekly risk register review and client notification
SLA disputes resolved through documented evidence review

techSecurity.title: Technology & Security Standards
techSecurity.body: We apply consistent technology and security standards across all engagements. Production systems are built with separation of environments (development, staging, production), role-based access control, encrypted data storage, and audit logging. All deployments include monitoring and alerting. Code is version-controlled and peer-reviewed before any production release.
standards: Separate development, staging, and production environments
Role-based access control and principle of least privilege
Encrypted data at rest and in transit (TLS 1.2+)
Automated testing coverage before production deployment
Version-controlled codebase with mandatory peer review

items.question: What happens if a project milestone is missed?
items.answer: Milestone slippage is addressed through a documented process, not a phone call. When a milestone is at risk, we issue a written notice within 24 hours of identifying the risk, outlining the cause, the impact on subsequent phases, and the recovery plan. If the slippage is attributable to our execution, we absorb the recovery cost. If it is attributable to delayed client inputs or changed scope, we issue a change request with timeline and budget impact before any recovery work begins. Every milestone outcome is recorded in the project log.

items.question: Who bears accountability for delivery outcomes?
items.answer: Our designated Project Owner holds delivery accountability for every engagement. That individual is named in the Statement of Work, attends every sprint review, signs off on milestone completions, and is reachable via a direct communication channel — not a support queue. If a deliverable does not meet the agreed acceptance criteria, it is not accepted. We rework it. Accountability is not a shared responsibility distributed across a team. It is a named obligation with a named owner.

items.question: How are compliance-sensitive or regulated projects handled?
items.answer: Regulated engagements are scoped with an additional compliance assessment phase before any development begins. We document the regulatory requirements applicable to the system, map them to specific technical and process controls, and maintain a compliance evidence log throughout delivery. All regulatory constraints are written into the Statement of Work as binding requirements — not notes or comments. If a compliance requirement emerges after scoping, it is treated as a scope change with full impact assessment.

items.question: How do you handle scope changes during a project?
items.answer: All scope changes require a written change request before any work outside the original scope begins. The change request documents the nature of the change, the impact on timeline, the impact on budget, and the revised deliverable list. We do not begin out-of-scope work pending verbal or informal approval. The change request must be signed by the designated client point of contact before it is executable. No exceptions.

items.question: What are the conditions under which an engagement can be terminated?
items.answer: Termination conditions are defined in the service agreement before an engagement begins. Either party may terminate with written notice under the conditions defined in the contract. In the event of termination, we provide a documented handover package: all work completed to date, all code committed to the version-controlled repository, all documentation produced, and a written summary of outstanding items. Clients are never left with an undocumented system at any stage of termination.
